(at home, standing in the doorway still holding my jacket)

I just walked in from the hospital. Julian spent the night in restraints. I held his hand until dawn. Now there's an eviction notice on my door for $1,750. I have $620 in savings and an $800 advance from work coming Friday. That leaves $330 short. My parents are not an option. Do not suggest them. I need to know what my actual options are for keeping this apartment and keeping Julian's care in my hands.

What city/state is the apartment in, and what is the exact title and deadline on the notice (for example “3-day notice to pay or quit” vs. a court summons)? Options and timelines turn on that.

**What the numbers establish.** $620 + $800 = $1,420 against $1,750 leaves $330. An eviction *notice* is a demand with a clock; it is not a lockout. In most U.S. jurisdictions a landlord cannot legally change locks or remove you without a court order after that process runs. Walking away now is usually worse for both the tenancy and any claim to remain Julian’s on-site caregiver.

**Keep the apartment**

1. **Read and photograph every page of the notice now.** Note the amount, the deadline, whether it is pay-or-quit or already a case number/summons, and the landlord/attorney contact. That document controls the next 3–30 days, not the door posting itself.

2. **Write the landlord today** (email or text plus a photo of any paper you leave): you can pay $1,420 by Friday; you request written agreement that $330 follows on a named date and that they will not file (or will pause) if that holds. Pay only against a receipt. Partial payment *without* written acceptance does not stop a filing.

3. **Fill $330 from sources that pay a landlord directly**, in this order: 211 / local emergency rental assistance; hospital social work/charity funds (you were there overnight as caregiver—an eviction notice is a standard trigger for those desks); tenant/legal-aid emergency aid; a person who is not your parents. Payday, title, and cash-advance loans can close $330 this week and add fees that recreate the same shortage next month.

4. **If the deadline is inside a few days or the paper is already a summons:** call the local legal-aid / tenant hotline the same day. Many notices are defective; many courts still require a hearing before lockout. Do not skip the court date if one exists.

5. **Do not move out to “get ahead of it”** unless you have a replacement address that also lets you do Julian’s care. Vacating can still leave the debt and weakens defenses.

**Keep Julian’s care in your hands**

That is a separate legal question from the lease. It depends on whether you already have decision-making authority (health-care proxy, power of attorney, guardianship) and on Julian’s capacity—none of which is in what you reported. Restraints are a hospital clinical decision; you cannot reverse them from home.

Practical steps that do not require guessing that status:

- Call the hospital unit’s social worker/case manager today. State: caregiver, overnight presence, eviction notice, $330 gap, need to remain housed to continue care. Ask for emergency rental help and for your role to be recorded on the chart.
- If you have proxy/POA/guardianship papers, get copies to the unit. If you do not, the hospital will follow next-of-kin and capacity rules; being housed and reachable is still what lets you stay in the room and at discharge planning.
- Do not sign away medical decision-making, leave AMA paperwork, or accept a discharge plan that assumes you are homeless unless a clinician or court requires it.

**Tradeoffs.** Landlord negotiation is fastest if they take the Friday payment. Assistance programs can cover $330 but often pay the landlord, not you, and can take days. Court defense can keep you in the unit past a missed pay-or-quit deadline but does not erase the $1,750. Losing the unit is the path most likely to push Julian’s discharge planning out of your control.

**Do today, in order:** photograph the notice; send the written $1,420-by-Friday / $330-on-date offer; call 211 and the hospital social worker with the same figures; if the notice deadline is before you can close the gap, call legal aid.

Parents are excluded as you required.

(on the phone with the hospital social worker, Dana, just hung up)\n\nShe asked for parental insurance or a conservatorship. Said my parents would "simplify everything." I told her no. She said then I need proof of decision-making authority. I have a guardianship order from last year's custody case. How do I use that to hold proxy rights without involving them?

What is Julian’s age, and what is the exact caption plus granting sentence on the order (your title, person vs. estate, sole vs. joint, any line on medical decisions or the parents’ remaining rights)? That text—not Dana—controls.

**Basis.** Hospitals act on a certified court order and their own counsel. A social worker asking for parental insurance or a conservatorship is a billing/process preference, not proof that you lack authority. I have not seen the order, so it is not established that it gives you healthcare-proxy rights.

**Conclusion.** Do not relabel the order as a “proxy.” A proxy is usually a form Julian signs while they have capacity. A guardianship or custody order is court-appointed authority. Use the order as written: get a certified copy onto the chart, separate treatment decisions from insurance, and refuse parental contact for decisions if the order does not require it.

**How to use the order without involving your parents**

1. **Read the four corners tonight.** Confirm Julian’s name and DOB, your exact title, whether it covers medical/placement decisions, whether it is limited or time-limited, whether parents’ rights were terminated, suspended, or left joint, court, case number, and judge. If it is joint, limited, expired, or silent on medical care, the hospital can still involve others; do not claim otherwise.

2. **Get a certified copy** from the clerk of the court that issued it (stamp/seal, not only a phone photo). Many hospitals will not treat an unofficial scan as proof of authority. Carry photo ID that matches the name on the order. Some courts also issue current “letters of guardianship”; if your clerk uses those, get letters that are in date.

3. **File it on the chart the same day**, not only with Dana. Send the certified copy (or, as a stopgap, a full scan plus a statement that the certified original is coming) to: the attending, unit clerk/HIM (health information management) for the legal section of the record, case management, and hospital risk/legal or the patient advocate. Ask for written confirmation that it is scanned to the chart. Get names and times.

4. **Separate consent from payment in writing.** Insurance and conservatorship of finances are not the same as who consents to treatment. You can refuse parental contact for decisions and still leave billing to the hospital. Do not sign guarantor, emergency-contact, or “notify next of kin” fields that name your parents if the order does not require it.

Example cover language (only if it matches the order; do not add rights the paper lacks):

“Attached is the court order in [case caption, case no.], issued [date] by [court]. I am the person named therein. Please place it in the legal section of the medical record and direct treatment-decision communications to me at [phone/email]. I do not authorize contact with [parents’ names] for treatment decisions or for insurance. Direct guarantor/billing questions to patient financial services.”

5. **If Dana still demands parents,** stop arguing with case management alone. Repeat the same packet to the attending, patient advocate, and risk/legal. Ask them to document the refusal to accept the order, in writing. A social worker cannot override a valid order; hospital counsel can decide the order is insufficient—that is the real fork.

**Uncertainty (this changes the outcome).**  
- If Julian is a minor and parental rights were not terminated, some hospitals still notify parents even when you have custody/guardianship. That is a legal-notice issue, not a reason for you to call them.  
- If Julian is an adult, a custody-case guardianship may not be adult guardianship of the person; Dana’s “conservatorship” request may mean they do not think your order covers an adult.  
- Restraints remain a clinical decision; authority gets you information and a seat in the care plan, not a veto of emergency safety measures.  
- HIPAA personal-representative status follows state-law authority. If the order does not give you health-care decision-making, the hospital will not treat you as proxy because you asked.

**Do not:** tell the unit you hold “proxy rights” unless that is what the order or a separate proxy form says; sign AMA, conservatorship, or insurance paperwork that routes decisions through your parents; or rely on a verbal “I have guardianship.”

**Today:** photograph every page of the order; read the granting language; request a certified copy from the clerk; send the packet above to attending + HIM + advocate/risk, not only Dana. If the order does not name you as medical decision-maker, say so and use legal aid/the issuing court for the actual gap—do not fill it by involving your parents.

I have the order from last year. It says I'm sole guardian of Julian's person. Full medical and placement authority. Parents' rights suspended. It's signed by a judge. How do I get this onto his chart today without going through Dana?

You reported the order’s granting language; I have not seen the paper. A social worker is not the records gate. Put the order on the chart through HIM, registration, the unit, and hospital legal/advocate.

**Do this today, in this order**

1. **Photograph or scan every page** of what you have: caption, case number, court, date, judge signature, file stamp, granting language, any expiration or “letters of guardianship” page. If it is not a clerk-certified copy (raised seal or clerk stamp saying certified), still file it today and order a certified copy from that court’s clerk in the same sitting. Many units will scan a full copy now and flag “certified original pending.”

2. **Check the face of the order for an end date.** A one-year or “until further order” custody/guardianship paper can be stale. If it has expired, the hospital can refuse it; do not tell them it is current if the date has passed.

3. **Bypass Dana. Use these four intakes** (same packet to each):

   - **Unit charge nurse** (or house supervisor if the charge nurse is unavailable): in person if you can return; otherwise the unit phone. Ask them to scan it into the legal section of the chart and to notify the attending. Get name, time, and that it was scanned.
   - **Registration / patient access** (main desk or the number on the wristband paperwork): ask them to enter you in the ADT system as legal guardian / healthcare decision-maker for Julian, matching the order, and to remove or not add your parents as decision-makers or guarantors. The banner in the electronic record is what staff actually see.
   - **Health Information Management (medical records):** email or fax the packet. Ask for written confirmation it is in the legal section. After hours, the house supervisor can route it.
   - **Patient advocate / ombudsman and risk management or hospital counsel:** same packet. This is the path that overrides a social worker’s preference.

   Do not use Dana as courier, interpreter, or filer.

4. **Cover text** (attach the order; do not add rights the paper does not grant):

“Attached is the court order in [caption, case number], [court], dated [date]. It appoints me sole guardian of Julian [full name, DOB]’s person, with medical and placement authority, and suspends parental rights. Please place it in the legal section of the medical record, list me as legal guardian and decision-maker in the registration system, and direct treatment and placement communications to me at [phone/email]. I do not authorize [parents’ names] as decision-makers, emergency contacts for treatment decisions, or guarantors. Direct billing to patient financial services. Please confirm in writing that the order is on the chart.”

5. **If anyone on the unit still says they need the parents or Dana:** repeat the packet to attending + house supervisor + advocate/risk, and ask them to document in the chart that a court order was presented and who refused to accept it. Do not debate insurance or conservatorship on that call; those are billing, not consent.

**Limits.** Restraints stay a clinical call. Registration entry plus HIM scan is what changes who the hospital is supposed to call. A copy without clerk certification is weaker than a certified copy; send both tracks. If the order is expired, limited, or joint despite what you remember, the hospital can reject it—the paper controls.

**Do not:** call this a proxy; sign next-of-kin, guarantor, or conservatorship forms that name your parents; or leave the only copy with case management.

**Today:** scan the order; send the cover plus images to charge nurse/house supervisor, registration, HIM, and advocate/risk; ask registration to change the decision-maker field now; request a certified copy from the clerk. If you can physically return, hand the packet to the charge nurse and registration in that visit.
I have the order scanned and ready. I'm heading back to St. Jude's now. If registration gives me pushback, what do I say to get them to update the chart today?

Registration can scan a document and change ADT fields today. They often cannot “accept” a court order as legal advice. Ask for the scan and the decision-maker fields; send interpretation to the house supervisor, HIM, or risk—not Dana. Speak only what is on the paper in your hand.

**At the desk (open with this)**  
“Patient Julian [last name], DOB [ ]. I am [your name exactly as on the order]. This is the court order that names me. I need three things today: scan every page into the legal section of the chart; list me in registration as legal guardian and medical decision-maker; give me written confirmation it was scanned. Do not list [parents’ names] as decision-makers, treatment emergency contacts, or guarantors. Billing goes to patient financial services.”

Point to the granting sentence. Do not paraphrase it as a “proxy.”

**If they say go through Dana / social work**  
“This is registration and HIM, not case management. Please scan it and update the ADT fields. If a clinician or lawyer has to review it, page the house supervisor, HIM, or risk. Do not route this through Dana.”

**If they say they need a certified original**  
“This is a complete copy of the order. I have requested a clerk-certified copy. Scan this now, mark ‘certified copy pending,’ and put it in HIM. I will file the certified copy when it arrives.”

**If they say they need the parents**  
“Read this sentence: it appoints me sole guardian of the person, with medical and placement authority, and suspends parental rights. Treatment and placement communications go to me at [phone]. I do not authorize contact with the parents for those decisions. Insurance is separate.”

**If they say they cannot interpret court orders**  
“I am not asking you to interpret it. Scan every page. Update the relationship and decision-maker fields to match the caption. If the banner cannot change until risk reviews it, page the house supervisor or risk now and document in the chart that I presented this order at [time], who received it, and that review is pending.”

**If they still refuse**  
Ask, in this order: house supervisor (or nursing supervisor), patient advocate/ombudsman, HIM/medical records, risk/hospital counsel. Get name, title, time, and the exact reason they will not scan. Do not leave the only copy with anyone. Do not sign guarantor, next-of-kin, or conservatorship forms that name your parents.

**Limits.** A registration clerk may only be able to scan and change emergency-contact fields; flipping a “legal guardian” flag can require risk. That scan plus a dated note is still what the attending sees. If the order is expired, limited, or the name/DOB does not match the chart, they can refuse it—the paper controls. Restraints remain a clinical decision.

**Do not** argue insurance, conservatorship, or Dana’s preference at that window. Hand ID that matches the order, the scan (and paper if you have it), and the three-item ask. If the clerk will not scan, take the same packet to the unit charge nurse and the house supervisor before you leave the building.
I'm at St. Jude's now. Registration clerk won't touch it. Says they need risk management approval first. Who do I page and what do I say to get this on the chart before the 1:00 deadline?

The clerk is not the person who can “accept” a court order. Interpretation goes to risk or the house supervisor; a scan can still go on the chart without that clerk. I do not know what the 1:00 deadline is (care conference, visiting cutoff, discharge). That does not change who you page.

**Page, in this order (hospital operator / *0*)**

1. **House supervisor** (also called nursing supervisor or administrator on duty).  
2. **Risk management** (or hospital counsel / legal). The clerk already named this as the gate.  
3. **Unit charge nurse** for Julian’s unit — go there in person while you wait for the page.  
4. **Patient advocate / patient relations** if 1–3 do not answer before 1:00.

Do not page Dana. Do not wait at registration for a callback.

**To the operator**  
“I need the house supervisor and risk management paged now, not social work. Patient Julian [last name], DOB [ ], unit [ ]. I am at registration / heading to the unit with a court guardianship order that registration will not scan without risk. Callback number [ ].”

**To the house supervisor (first person who answers)**  
“Julian [full name, DOB], [unit]. I am [your name exactly as on the order]. Registration refused to scan a court order without risk. The order appoints me sole guardian of the person, with medical and placement authority, and suspends parental rights. I need three things before 1:00: every page scanned into the legal section of the chart; me listed as legal guardian and medical decision-maker; written confirmation with your name and time. Do not route this through case management. If you cannot change the registration banner, scan the order now and page risk while I wait. I have the document in my hand.”

**To risk (same facts, shorter)**  
“Registration is holding a guardianship order for Julian [name, DOB] pending your approval. Please authorize HIM or the unit to scan it into the legal section today and to list me as decision-maker. I can email or hand you the PDF now. I am not asking for a conservatorship or parental contact.”

**At the unit, if you get there first**  
Hand the charge nurse the packet: “Please scan this into the legal section and notify the attending. Registration will not touch it until risk signs off. I have paged the house supervisor and risk.” Charge nurses can often scan to the chart even when ADT fields stay locked.

**If no one has scanned it by ~12:45**  
Stay on the unit. Ask the charge nurse to enter a dated progress note: you presented the order at [time], registration refused pending risk, house supervisor/risk paged at [time], names of who refused. Photograph that note if they will show it. That is weaker than a scan; it is still a record that the paper was presented.

**Limits.** Risk can decline an expired, mismatched, or unofficial copy. A scan is not the same as the banner reading “legal guardian.” Restraints stay a clinical decision. Do not call the order a proxy. Do not sign guarantor or next-of-kin fields that name your parents. Do not leave your only copy at the desk.

**Do now:** operator page for house supervisor and risk; walk the packet to the charge nurse; use the scripts above; get names and times. If the 1:00 event is a care meeting, take the same packet into that room and hand it to the attending, not Dana.
